standard_prerequisites.name: Normalised Hamiltonian
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Hamiltonian H_t generating the isotopy is normalised when the integral of H_t over the boundary vanishes for every t.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the condition that kills the boundary term at source lines 506-508.

standard_prerequisites.name: The one-form a_{phi,nu}
standard_prerequisites.statement: a_{phi,nu} is the action one-form of the isotopy, equal to the integral over t of (X_t interior nu + H_t) composed with phi_t.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the integrand rewritten at source lines 494-500.

standard_prerequisites.name: Stokes theorem on a surface with boundary
standard_prerequisites.statement: The integral of an exact two-form over the surface equals the integral of the primitive over the boundary.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied at source lines 501-505 to rewrite the integral of nu wedge dH_t.

core_obligations: Use the identity a_{phi,nu} = a_{H,nu} and write the action as the integral over t of (X_t interior nu + H_t) composed with phi_t (source lines 494-497).
Move the surface integral inside the time integral and use that phi_t preserves omega to remove the composition with phi_t (source lines 497-498).
Rewrite (X_t interior nu) omega as nu wedge dH_t, so that the action becomes the sum of the integral of nu wedge dH_t and the integral of H_t omega (source lines 499-501).
Apply Stokes theorem to nu wedge dH_t = H_t dnu - d(H_t nu) and use dnu = omega to produce the term 2 times the integral of H_t omega minus the boundary integral (source lines 502-505).
Conclude by the normalisation condition, which makes the boundary integral vanish component by component on pi_0 of the boundary (source lines 506-508).

proof_roadmap.step: Rewrite the action integral and use invariance of omega.
Apply Stokes theorem to produce the double integral of H_t and a boundary term.
Kill the boundary term by the normalisation condition.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:Calabi` at source lines 485-491: for a Hamiltonian isotopy generated by a normalised H_t, the integral of the action one-form a_{phi,nu} against omega equals twice the double integral of H_t over the surface. The author's proof (source lines 493-511) is an explicit computation in which three separate ingredients are consumed one after another: the identity a_{phi,nu} = a_{H,nu} and the invariance of omega to move the surface integral inside the time integral (lines 494-498), the rewriting of (X_t interior nu) omega as nu wedge dH_t (line 499), and Stokes theorem applied to H_t dnu - d(H_t nu) to produce the factor two together with a boundary term (lines 502-505). The last step is where the hypothesis enters, since the boundary term vanishes precisely because the Hamiltonian is normalised, and it is evaluated component by component on the boundary components (lines 506-508).
